name: Nigeria

facts.religion: Muslim about half, Christian about half

snapshot: Africa's most populous country learned in January 2026 how close a 2025 coup plot came to killing its president, as insecurity spread across north and south.
culture: Nigeria is Africa's cultural superpower. Nollywood is one of the world's largest film industries by output, and Afrobeats stars like Burna Boy, Wizkid and Tems fill stadiums worldwide. Its writers, from Chinua Achebe and Wole Soyinka to Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, define African literature. More than 500 languages are spoken, with Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo the largest.
society: Lagos is one of Africa's biggest cities and its fintech capital. Oil dominates exports, but the end of fuel subsidies in 2023 and a currency collapse pushed inflation above 30 percent. Jihadists in the north-east, bandit gangs that kidnap for ransom in the north-west, herder-farmer violence and separatists in the south-east strain the army.
situation: Nigeria spent most of its first 40 years of independence under military rule, with six successful coups between 1966 and 1993. Since 1999 it has been a democracy, with power changing hands at the ballot box. In 2026, Nigerians learned how close that came to ending.

On 29 September 2025, the government abruptly cancelled the military parade for the 65th Independence Day. Officials denied any coup plot. Only in January 2026 did the military admit it: officers had planned to seize power and, investigators said, to kill President Bola Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shettima, the Senate president and the House speaker (Premium Times via AllAfrica). Some 40 suspects were identified, including officers, a police inspector and civilians accused of funding and propaganda; a Nollywood filmmaker was arrested as an alleged "propagandist," and a former oil minister, Timipre Sylva, accused of bankrolling the plot, remains at large (The Star). Six civilians were indicted in April and 36 military personnel went before a court martial in May. Analysts say the bigger story is why the plot was hidden, and what it says about an army fighting jihadists in the northeast, bandits in the northwest and separatists in the southeast with mixed success; one told RFI security "has never been worse" (RFI via AllAfrica). US drones and troops now help with intelligence. Tinubu, whose reforms ended fuel subsidies and sent prices soaring, is running for a second term in 2027.
power: A federal presidential republic of 36 states. The president is directly elected for four years with a two-term limit and must win a quarter of the vote in two-thirds of the states; the National Assembly has a Senate and a House. State governors are powerful.
holders: President Bola Tinubu (APC), in office since 2023.

conflicts.name: Jihadist spillover into coastal West Africa (Benin, Togo)
Northeast Nigeria jihadist insurgency (ISWAP and Boko Haram)
Northwest Nigeria banditry, Lakurawa and the Kainji-Borgu jihadist belt
Middle Belt communal and herder-farmer violence (Plateau, Benue, southern Kaduna)
